text:
A: Hello! Tomasz, from Walsall. You're Karen, yeah?
B: Yeah. Hi. Taunton.
A: Taunton, okay. Everybody today is Somerset or London. What do you do, Karen?
B: I manage a charity shop. Hospice one.
A: Charity shop! Listen, I go car boot every Sunday, I know this business. You buy cheap, you sell more, yeah?
B: Not really. People give it us for nothing. We price it, sell it, money goes to the hospice.
A: Okay, but same idea. Pricing. You know what something is worth.
B: Suppose so, yeah. I'm quick at it. Have to be, Monday morning there's thirty bags in the back.
A: Thirty bags! What's the best thing you found?
B: Erm, there was a Burberry coat once, proper one, not a fake. Went for ninety quid. And there's a lot of rubbish. False teeth.
A: (laughs) Teeth? Who gives teeth?
B: No idea. Bag of cardigans, teeth at the bottom.
A: Listen, people in your shop, they try to haggle? Because me, I would. You say a fiver, I say three.
B: They do, yeah. And I say no. It's for a hospice. You're haggling with people who are dying, basically.
A: Okay, okay. (laughs) Fair. In charity shop, I pay what it says. In car boot, no mercy. Last week I got drill set, a fiver, I sell for twenty-five.
B: That's the car boot, though. Different.
A: Yeah, different. So you are manager, how many people?
B: About twenty volunteers. Rota's a nightmare. Saturdays, nobody turns up.
A: Same in call centre! Monday, Friday, everybody is sick. Funny how they are sick only on Friday, yeah? I tell my team leader, sack them. He doesn't listen.
B: Can't sack volunteers. That's the trouble. I just end up doing it all myself, then I'm short with them.
A: Short is good. You tell them, they come next time.
B: Sometimes. Sometimes they don't come back at all. Then I feel bad.
A: Don't feel bad. Work is work. Look, I get people swear at me fifty times a day, I sleep like baby.
B: Lucky you.
A: What you do apart from shop?
B: Sewing, mostly. Mending, upcycling. Walking on the Quantocks. Garden, tomatoes.
A: Tomatoes, my wife's mum in Poland, whole garden, tomatoes, cucumbers, she makes pickles. Me, I do barbecue. That's it.
B: Right.
A: You sell your sewing? Online, eBay, Vinted? Listen, there's money in it. Upcycle, you put nice photos, you sell for double.
B: I keep meaning to. Never get round to it.
A: You must! Start this week. I tell you, if I can sew, I would be rich. You have the product, you just need sales. That's me, sales.
B: (laughs) Are you offering?
A: For ten per cent, why not? Listen, first thing, photos, good light —
